test_title: PYST 19: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 18 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question:
A shopkeeper offers the following discount schemes for buyers.

I. Two successive discounts of 15% and 20%

II. Successive discount of 25 % and 10%

III. A discount of 33%

The selling price will be minimum under the scheme:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective discount formula = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100

Discount I = 15 + 20 − (15 × 20) ÷ 100 = 32%

Discount II = 25 + 10 − (25 × 10) ÷ 100 = 32.5%

Discount III = 33%

Selling price is minimum when discount is maximum, which is 33%.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme III.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three discount schemes:

I. Successive discounts of 15% and 20%

II. Successive discount of 25% and 10%

III. A discount of 33%

**Formula Used:**

Effective Discount = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c94657fbcb46655d5875ab0608b4960760ec6d31095893b74f58ee609a916aa5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Scheme I Discount = 15 + 20 − (15 × 20) ÷ 100 = 35 − 3 = 32%

⇒ Scheme I Selling Price = 100% − 32% = 68% of Marked Price

⇒ Scheme II Discount = 25 + 10 − (25 × 10) ÷ 100 = 35 − 2.5 = 32.5%

⇒ Scheme II Selling Price = 100% − 32.5% = 67.5% of Marked Price

⇒ Scheme III Discount = 33%

⇒ Scheme III Selling Price = 100% − 33% = 67% of Marked Price

⇒ Comparing the Selling Prices: 67% [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts x% and y% are given consecutively on an item, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

The selling price is calculated after applying the discount on the marked price. It can be found directly using the formula: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Maximising Discount for Consumer

For a consumer, if the sum of successive discounts given in different schemes is the same, the sequence with the largest numerical difference between the individual discounts always yields a higher overall discount.
